To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a quantitative real-time PCR (qRT- PCR) assay targeting the internal transcriber spacer 1- 5.8S ribosomal RNA gene of Alexandrium minutum Global Clade (GC) was developed and used to detect and enumerate A. minutum GC in seawater samples in Cork Harbour, in the summer of 2007, in comparison with whole-cell FISH analysis and morphotaxonomic methods.
a quantitative real-time PCR (qRT- PCR) assay targeting the internal trans-cribed spacer 1 (ITS1) of the rRNA operon of the potentially toxic species A. minutum was developed.
the qRT-PCR method is a rapid, sensitive, specific and reproducible method for the detection and enumeration of the potentially toxic microalga A. minutum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and evaluating molecular techniques for the detection and enumeration of potentially toxic microalgae.
the development of a qRT-PCR for the detection and enumeration of the toxic Alexandrium minutum.

the development of a rapid, specific and sensitive qRT-PCR for the detection and enumeration of A. minutum in the field and the evaluation of qRT-PCR against WC-FISH and conventional morphological analyses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the qRT-PCR method is a suitable tool for the detection and enumeration of A. minutum, but the WC-FISH method should be used for the identification of the species.
the qRT-PCR method is a suitable tool for the quantification of A. minutum GC in seawater samples and is as effective as WC-FISH and traditional morphological methods.
qPCR, WC-FIS and morphology all have their place in the analysis of Alexandrium minutum populations, and the choice of methodology will depend on the specific requirements of the study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
qRT-PCR and WC-FISH can be used as complementary methods to morphotaxonomy to detect, enumerate and monitor A. minutum in the field.
qRT-PCR is the most sensitive and specific method for detection of the species.

the qRT-PCR method was a reliable and rapid tool for the enumeration and monitoring of Alexandrium minutum, and that the WC-FISH method was an effective tool for the enumeration of Alexandrium species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
qRT-PCR is a useful tool for the detection and enumeration of A. minutum in environmental samples, especially where other molecular tools such as WC-FISH may be difficult to implement.

molecular methods can be developed to detect and quantify toxic microalgae in the field and that these methods may provide a more accurate assessment of population dynamics compared to traditional methods.
the qRT-PCR approach for A. minutm (GC) is a promising tool for the detection, quantification and monitoring of this species.
